titles.title: Deformation mechanisms of selective laser melted 316L austenitic stainless steel in high temperature low cycle fatigue

descriptions.description: Publisher Copyright: © 2022 Elsevier B.V.

To investigate the low cycle fatigue (LCF) properties of SLM (Selective laser melting) 316L at 550 °C high temperature, a series of LCF tests at different strain amplitudes is conducted on SLM 316L and traditional 316L. In contrast to the cyclic hardening behavior of traditional 316L, SLM 316L is shown to have a stable cyclic softening behavior and higher fatigue life due to its higher strength (yield strength is 1.9 times of traditional 316L). The coarsening of cellular sub-structure, evolution of geometrically necessary dislocations (GND) and texture direction contribute to the cyclic softening behavior of SLM 316L. Fractographic observations illustrate that strain amplitude has a significant influence on initiation and propagation of transgranular fatigue cracks, and lack-of-fusion defects near the surface are key initiation sites of fatigue cracks. Additionally, the life prediction method of the non-Masing model is suitable for SLM 316L.

titles.title: Microstructure-sensitive prediction and experimental validation of fretting fatigue

descriptions.description: This paper is concerned with the development of a micro-mechanical methodology for prediction of fretting fatigue crack nucleation life and short crack propagation. The methodology employs critical accumulated plastic slip as a fatigue indicator parameter for microstructure-sensitive crack nucleation. Crystal plasticity unit-cell models are employed for calibration of constitutive and crack nucleation parameters and a crystal plasticity frictional contact model of the fretting test rig is developed to predict the micro-scale surface fretting damage, crack nucleation and estimated micro-crack propagation. The methodology is validated against fretting fatigue tests using a fretting bridge arrangement for 316L stainless steel. eneral agreemen between the FE predicted and experimental fretting fatigue lives.

titles.title: A physically-based fatigue model and experimental testing for PBF-LB 316L

descriptions.description: Publisher Copyright: © IMechE 2025

This work examines the effect of build orientation and post-build machining on tensile and fatigue behaviour of stainless steel (SS) 316L specimens produced by laser beam powder bed fusion (PBF-LB). X-ray diffraction and tensile and fatigue testing are used to investigate residual stresses and fatigue. The results demonstrated: (i) horizontal builds are stronger but less ductile than vertical builds, and (ii) effect of machining on tensile and fatigue behaviour, namely, increasing yield, tensile and fatigue strength but decreasing ductility. Effect of orientation was more pronounced for as-built specimens. Significant benefit of machining for fatigue was attributed to reduced surface roughness and compressive residual stresses. This work adapts and verifies the physically-based Tanaka-Mura (T-M) fatigue crack initiation model for PBF-LB SS316L. The model captures the beneficial effects of machining via measured surface roughness and residual stresses for both horizontally- and vertically-built specimens.

titles.title: Micromechanical modelling of fatigue crack nucleation in stents

descriptions.description: A finite element based micro-mechanical methodology for cyclic plasticity and fatigue crack initiation in cardiovascular stents is presented. The methodology is based on the combined use of a (global) three-dimensional continuum stent-artery model, a local micromechanical stent model, the development of a combined kinematic- isotropic hardening crystal plasticity constitutive formulation, and the application of micro- structure sensitive crack initiation parameters. The methodology is applied to 316L stainless steel stents with random polycrystalline microstructures, based on scanning electron microscopy images of the grain morphology, under realistic elastic-plastic loading histories, including crimp, deployment and in-vivo systolic-diastolic cyclic pressurisation. Identification of the micro- mechanical cyclic plasticity and failure constants is achieved via application of an objective function and a unit cell representative volume element for 316L stainless steel. Cyclic stent deformations are compared with the J2 -predicted response and conventional fatigue life prediction techniques. It is shown that micro- mechanical fatigue analysis of stents is necessary due to the significant predicted effects of material inhomogeneity on micro-plasticity and micro-crack initiation.

descriptions.description: Additively manufactured (AM) components—either made by laser-powder bed fusion or wire and arc additive manufacturing—typically contain process-related defects on and near surfaces that can be removed by machining. Various studies have shown that post-treatment, such as machining significantly improves the fatigue strength of AM parts. To this day, however, hardly any studies have investigated the fatigue strength of post-treated additively manufactured components with notches. In this study, fatigue tests were performed on plain and notched specimens to determine and compare the crack initiation and crack propagation behavior due to different manufacturing-related effects. Tests were performed on specimens produced by the two aforementioned AM processes and compared to specimens taken from wrought sheets. The fatigue strength of AM materials is influenced by microstructure, defects, residual stress, and notches. PBF-LB/M specimens exhibit the highest fatigue strength in plain, notch-free conditions, attributed to differences in microstructure and static strength affecting fatigue crack initiation. Notched specimens show larger differences among materials, with PBF-LB/M having shorter fatigue crack propagation life related to line-type defect clusters, while the plain PBF-LB/M specimens are less affected as their fatigue strength is primarily determined by fatigue crack initiation.

titles.title: The effect of grain orientation on fretting fatigue plasticity and life prediction

descriptions.description: A study on crystal and J2 plasticity prediction of fretting fatigue is presented, using a microstructure-sensitive fatigue parameter for crystal plasticity crack nucleation and a critical-plane (multiaxial) fatigue parameter for J2 plasticity. A short crack propagation methodology is also implemented. The effect of grain orientation on nucleation life is shown to be significant for fretting fatigue. J2 plasticity generally predicts conservative lives. Crystal plasticity is superior in terms of (i) accuracy of life prediction, (ii) ability to facilitate wear prediction and (iii) capturing the key effects of substrate fatigue stress and grain orientation on life. The crystal plasticity model facilitates new insight into interaction between grain orientation, fatigue stress amplitude and fretting surface damage vis-à-vis fretting fatigue life.

titles.title: Strain Mapping in the Vicinity of Cracks Using a Conical Slit Setup for Angular Dispersive Synchrotron X-Ray Diffraction

descriptions.description: Background Laser-based powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) is a manufacturing technique that enables tailoring of the propertiesof components towards the application, provided the process parameters are adjusted. However, the process inducesresidual strain and stresses, influencing, i.e., the fatigue properties. To analyze the residual strain distributions in the vicinityof fatigue cracks in the bulk of specimens a high lateral resolution is necessary, which limits the possible analysis methodsto high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction.Objective The objective is to propose a viable strategy to determine the (lattice) strain distributions in the vicinity of fatiguecracks in AISI 316L compact-tension specimens manufactured via PBF-LB/M.Methods An angular dispersive high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction setup with conical slits is used, to restrict thegauge volume to the center of the specimens. Complementarily, the residual stress distribution near the surface is investigatedusing the incremental hole-drilling method.Results Along the build direction a compressive residual strain distribution of higher magnitude is found, which is significantlyreduced in the vicinity of the crack. Depending on whether the crack opening direction is aligned with the transverseor the build direction, a tensile lattice strain field or a lattice strain field of reduced magnitude is found ahead of the crack tip.Conclusions The results indicate that the proposed strategy is well suited to determine the (lattice) strain distributions in thevicinity of fatigue cracks in the center of the specimens with a sufficient lateral resolution.

titles.title: Failure Mode of Transcondylar Screws Used for Treatment of Incomplete Ossification of the Humeral Condyle in 5 Dogs

descriptions.description: To investigate the mode of failure of transcondylar screws retrieved from dogs previously treated for incomplete ossification of the humeral condyle (IOHC). Metallurgical study. Broken screws (n=5) from dogs with IOHC. Broken transcondylar bone screws were retrieved from dogs that had apparently successful surgery for IOHC. Screws were measured and examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive analysis by X-rays (EDX). EDX confirmed that screws were made from 316L stainless steel and there was no evidence of significant corrosion or manufacturing faults that might have contributed to implant failure. SEM of the fractured surface of screws revealed a similar and complex pattern of fatigue failure characterized by multidirectional fatigue cracks and the presence of several initiation sites. All screws had signs of fatigue failure because of multidirectional forces of variable magnitude. Intercondylar instability is a feature of IOHC that persists despite placement of a transcondylar screw. The pathogenesis of IOHC involves chronic intercondylar instability and its treatment using even relatively large transcondylar screws has a risk of late implant failure.

titles.title: HE-Austenite: Hydrogen Embrittlement of Austenitic Stainless Steels in Gaseous Hydrogen, Separating Weld Metal from Base metal, with Per-Heat Composition

descriptions.description:
Hydrogen Embrittlement in Austenetic Stainless Steels: an open dataset of hydrogen embrittlement in austenitic stainless steels in gaseous hydrogen, with weld zone and per-heat composition

 An open dataset of hydrogen embrittlement in austenitic stainless steels tested in hydrogen gas, with the weld zone and the published composition recorded for every record.

113 records · 45 fields · 9 sources, 1983–2024 · Data CC BY 4.0 · Code MIT

Values were extracted by hand from published tables. No new experiments were performed, and no source document is redistributed here.

Objective

Hydrogen infrastructure is welded. Refuelling stations run at 70 MPa, storage vessels and tube trailers are welded assemblies, and repurposing existing pipe networks depends on how the joints behave rather than the plate. A weld is a casting sitting inside a wrought product: dendritic, different in composition from the parent metal, and deliberately holding a few percent of delta ferrite to avoid solidification cracking. It is the part of a joint least like the material a designer looked up, and the part hydrogen reaches first.

Most published embrittlement data covers base metal, and most recent weld studies charge specimens electrochemically, which cannot be converted to an equivalent gas pressure without assumptions about charging efficiency. This dataset keeps only gaseous exposure and records the weld zone for every row.

SCOPE

A record is included when the material is an austenitic stainless steel or a related grade flagged by material_family (duplex 2507, A286); hydrogen was introduced as a gas, either by testing in high-pressure hydrogen or by thermal precharging in hydrogen gas; a reference measurement exists from the same study and material, in air, helium, nitrogen, argon or the uncharged condition; and the value appears in a table rather than only in a figure.

Coverage: 228 to 423 K, and 0.1 to 172 MPa hydrogen for the 104 records whose source stated a pressure.

Electrochemically charged studies are excluded, because hydrogen fugacity from cathodic charging cannot be converted to an equivalent gas pressure without assumptions. They are listed with the reason in the Extraction log sheet of the workbook, alongside sources identified too late for this release.

WHAT ONE RECORD IS

One record is one reported test condition and one property: an alloy and heat, a weld zone, a hydrogen exposure, a test temperature and strain rate, the property measured in the reference environment, the property measured in or after hydrogen, and the ratio of the two. Where the property is reduction of area, that ratio is the relative reduction of area, RRA.

WHAT IS IN THIS VERSION

Per-heat composition for 102 of 113 records, as ten element columns in weight percent, with composition_basis saying whether the value is a measured heat analysis or a nominal composition, and composition_source naming the exact table it was read from. A composition is attached to a record only when the source reports it for the same heat, weld deposit or filler as the mechanical test, and a specification range is never recorded as a measurement.

A nickel equivalent recomputed for every record from one expression, Hirayama's six-element form, Ni + 0.65 Cr + 0.98 Mo + 1.05 Mn + 0.35 Si + 12.6 C, covering 93 records. Where a source printed its own value on a different expression it is kept separately in ni_equivalent_reported rather than mixed into the recomputed column.

Angel Md30 for the 55 records whose composition falls inside the range that expression was fitted on. Outside that range the linear form returns temperatures below absolute zero, which is a sign that it does not apply rather than a measure of stability, so it is not computed there.

The recomputed nickel equivalent reproduces four values the sources themselves print — Nakamura et al. (2018) heats P and a, and Fukunaga (2024) SUS316CW and A286 — exactly.

WHAT THE DATA SHOWS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

Relative reduction of area is the value measured in or after hydrogen divided by the value in the reference environment. A value of 1.0 means no measurable loss. Japanese regulatory practice accepts austenitic stainless steels for hydrogen service at RRA greater than or equal to 0.80.

Zone and alloy family are not independent in this dataset, so they have to be read together. Pooled across all families, base metal sits at a median RRA of 0.85 over 36 records and weld metal at 0.49 over 14, but those two groups are not comparable head to head: the weld-metal records come from three sources and 12 of the 14 are type 304 family, while the base-metal records span eight families and include the more stable grades. Within the type 304 family the comparison is 0.72 against 0.48, and within types 316 and 317 it is 0.99 against 0.73 on two weld records.

Ductility retained rises with the nickel equivalent: Spearman rho = 0.60 across the 24 distinct heats, weld deposits and fillers behind the 54 reduction-of-area records that carry a composition, p = 0.002. Statistics are quoted per material rather than per record because eight of the Sandia composite weld rows share a single fusion-zone analysis. The criterion Ni_eq greater than or equal to 26.3, proposed by Matsuoka et al., separates 10 materials at a median RRA of 0.64 from 14 at 0.95.

That relationship holds between alloy families and not within one. The low band is 26 of 27 records from the type 304 family, and within that family alone, where nine materials span Ni_eq 23.0 to 26.5, the relationship disappears, rho = -0.12, p = 0.77. It is not an artefact of the mixed reference environments: restricting to air and helium references leaves rho = 0.63 across 18 materials, p = 0.005. Md30 carries no relationship with ductility retained inside its valid range, rho = -0.42, p = 0.13.

Welds sit below base metal inside both nickel-equivalent bands, 0.71 against 0.47 below 26.3 and 0.99 against 0.86 at or above it, which argues that the zone effect is not only a composition effect. Each weld cell rests on three weld deposits, so this is a direction worth testing rather than a quantity worth citing.

DELTA FERRITE

Nakamura et al. (2018) tested one TIG-welded bar three ways at 228 K in 106 MPa hydrogen against a nitrogen reference: 316 high-nickel base metal at RRA 1.02, 317L weld metal as welded at 0.55, and the same weld metal after a post-weld solution treatment at 0.91. One material, one gas, one temperature, with the treatment that dissolves the ferrite as the variable.

This reading is contested and the dataset cannot settle it. Hirata (2015) reports RRA against delta ferrite ratio for ten weld metals in 45 MPa hydrogen gas and concludes the opposite, that weld-metal embrittlement is governed by austenite stability rather than by delta ferrite. That study reports its results only in figures and is therefore not included here. The ferrite_number field is populated for 2 of 113 records, so nobody should model ferrite content against ductility from this release.

KNOWN LIMITS

Identification, screening and extraction were done by one person. There was no second independent screener, so screening error cannot be quantified. 24 of 113 records were independently re-extracted from the source documents and matched; those rows are marked verified = yes.

The heat affected zone and the fusion line are defined in the zone vocabulary but carry no records.

Reference environments are mixed: 48 records against air, 28 against high-pressure helium, 32 against the uncharged condition, 5 against nitrogen or argon. A helium reference at test pressure is stricter than an air reference, and the field is recorded so users can filter. Twelve of the 14 weld-metal records use an uncharged reference.

Eleven records carry no composition because their source names no heat; they are left empty rather than filled from a specification.

The Sandia 304L heat W69 is published with C = 0.20 wt%, far outside the 304L specification and almost certainly a typographical error in the source. It is recorded as printed and flagged, and it raises that heat's nickel equivalent by about 2.2. One record uses it.

Weld compositions are the fusion zone or filler analysis the source gives. Dilution of the filler by the parent plate is not accounted for anywhere, because no source in this set reports it.

Family medians for types 321 and 347 (n = 3), type 310 (n = 2), duplex (n = 2) and A286 (n = 1) rest on few records and are indicative only.

SOURCES

Caskey GR Jr. Hydrogen Compatibility Handbook for Stainless Steels. DP-1643, Savannah River Laboratory, June 1983. https://www.osti.gov/biblio/5906050

San Marchi C, Somerday BP (eds). Technical Reference on Hydrogen Compatibility of Materials. SAND2012-7321, Sandia National Laboratories, 2012. https://h2tools.org/technical-reference

Balch DK, San Marchi C, et al. Effect of hydrogen on tensile strength and ductility of multipass 304L/308L welds. PVP2015-45591, ASME, 2015.

Michler T, Lee Y, Gangloff RP, Naumann J. Influence of macro segregation on hydrogen environment embrittlement of SUS 316L. International Journal of Hydrogen Energy 34(7) 2009, 3201-3209. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijhydene.2009.02.015

Nakamura J, Okazaki S, Matsunaga H, Matsuoka S. SSRT and fatigue life properties of 317L weld metal in high-pressure hydrogen gas. Transactions of the JSME 84(857) 2018, in Japanese. https://doi.org/10.1299/transjsme.17-00437

Younes CM, Steele AM, Nicholson JA, Barnett CJ. Influence of hydrogen content on the tensile properties and fracture of austenitic stainless steel welds. International Journal of Hydrogen Energy 38 2013, 4864-4876.

Iyer KJL. The influence of hydrogen on the mechanical properties and structure of a stable 304 stainless steel. Canadian Metallurgical Quarterly 28(2) 1989, 153. https://doi.org/10.1179/cmq.1989.28.2.153

Fukunaga A. Hydrogen embrittlement behaviours during SSRT tests in gaseous hydrogen for cold-worked type 316 and A286 used in hydrogen refuelling stations. Engineering Failure Analysis 160 2024, 108158. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engfailanal.2024.108158

Matsuoka S, Yamabe J, Matsunaga H. Hydrogen-induced ductility loss of austenitic stainless steels for slow strain rate tensile testing in high-pressure hydrogen gas. Solid State Phenomena 258 2017, 259-264. https://doi.org/10.4028/www.scientific.net/SSP.258.259

FILES IN THIS DEPOSIT

he_austenite_v0.2.csv — the dataset, 113 records, 45 fieldsHE-Austenite_v0.2.xlsx — the same rows plus summary, data dictionary, sources and extraction log sheetscompositions.csv — one row per heat, weld deposit or filler, with the table each composition came fromrecord_composition_map.csv — which record uses which compositionrecords_raw.json — the raw extraction records with full provenance notesdata_dictionary.md — every column, its meaning and its completenessschema.json — the record schemanormalise.py, apply_compositions.py, build_outputs.py, build_workbook.py, make_figures.py — the pipelinefig1_family.png, fig2_pressure.png, fig3_ferrite.png, fig4_nieq.png — the figuresREADME.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CITATION.cff, LICENSE, LICENSE-DATA.txt, requirements.txt

The pipeline reproduces the released CSV byte for byte from a clean copy, in the order normalise, apply_compositions, build_outputs, build_workbook, make_figures.

CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS VERSION

The first release, deposited in September 2026, carried no composition data and a nickel equivalent for only 14 records. This version adds composition for 102 records, recomputes the nickel equivalent for 93 on a single expression, and adds Md30 for 55. No mechanical property, ratio or record identifier changed, so analysis built on the previous version still runs.

REPOSITORY

https://github.com/mfaizansworkspace-ai/Hydrogen-Embrittlement-in-Austenitic-Stainless-Steels 

Corrections and contributions are welcome. CONTRIBUTING.md gives the column spec, the provenance rules and how credit is handled. If a value here disagrees with the source in front of you, open an issue with the record identifier, the value in the dataset, the value you read and the table it came from.

HOW TO CITE

Faizan, M. (2026). HE-Austenite: hydrogen embrittlement of austenitic stainlesssteels in gaseous hydrogen, separating weld metal from base metal, with per-heatcomposition (v0.2) [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23107694

Numbered style:

M. Faizan, HE-Austenite: Hydrogen Embrittlement of Austenitic Stainless Steels in Gaseous Hydrogen, Separating Weld Metal from Base metal, with Per-Heat Composition, Zenodo (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23107694.

10.5281/zenodo.23107694 points to this version and its exact numbers. The conceptDOI 10.5281/zenodo.22922356 always resolves to the newest version; use it when youmean the dataset in general. If your results depend on the values, cite the version.

CITATION.cff in the repository carries the same details in machine-readable form.

Hydrogen Embrittlement in Austenetic Stainless Steels: an open dataset of hydrogen embrittlement in austenitic stainless steels in gaseous hydrogen, with weld zone and per-heat composition

 An open dataset of hydrogen embrittlement in austenitic stainless steels tested in hydrogen gas, with the weld zone and the published composition recorded for every record.

113 records · 45 fields · 9 sources, 1983–2024 · Data CC BY 4.0 · Code MIT

Values were extracted by hand from published tables. No new experiments were performed, and no source document is redistributed here.

Objective

Hydrogen infrastructure is welded. Refuelling stations run at 70 MPa, storage vessels and tube trailers are welded assemblies, and repurposing existing pipe networks depends on how the joints behave rather than the plate. A weld is a casting sitting inside a wrought product: dendritic, different in composition from the parent metal, and deliberately holding a few percent of delta ferrite to avoid solidification cracking. It is the part of a joint least like the material a designer looked up, and the part hydrogen reaches first.

Most published embrittlement data covers base metal, and most recent weld studies charge specimens electrochemically, which cannot be converted to an equivalent gas pressure without assumptions about charging efficiency. This dataset keeps only gaseous exposure and records the weld zone for every row.

SCOPE

A record is included when the material is an austenitic stainless steel or a related grade flagged by material_family (duplex 2507, A286); hydrogen was introduced as a gas, either by testing in high-pressure hydrogen or by thermal precharging in hydrogen gas; a reference measurement exists from the same study and material, in air, helium, nitrogen, argon or the uncharged condition; and the value appears in a table rather than only in a figure.

Coverage: 228 to 423 K, and 0.1 to 172 MPa hydrogen for the 104 records whose source stated a pressure.

Electrochemically charged studies are excluded, because hydrogen fugacity from cathodic charging cannot be converted to an equivalent gas pressure without assumptions. They are listed with the reason in the Extraction log sheet of the workbook, alongside sources identified too late for this release.

WHAT ONE RECORD IS

One record is one reported test condition and one property: an alloy and heat, a weld zone, a hydrogen exposure, a test temperature and strain rate, the property measured in the reference environment, the property measured in or after hydrogen, and the ratio of the two. Where the property is reduction of area, that ratio is the relative reduction of area, RRA.

WHAT IS IN THIS VERSION

Per-heat composition for 102 of 113 records, as ten element columns in weight percent, with composition_basis saying whether the value is a measured heat analysis or a nominal composition, and composition_source naming the exact table it was read from. A composition is attached to a record only when the source reports it for the same heat, weld deposit or filler as the mechanical test, and a specification range is never recorded as a measurement.

A nickel equivalent recomputed for every record from one expression, Hirayama's six-element form, Ni + 0.65 Cr + 0.98 Mo + 1.05 Mn + 0.35 Si + 12.6 C, covering 93 records. Where a source printed its own value on a different expression it is kept separately in ni_equivalent_reported rather than mixed into the recomputed column.

Angel Md30 for the 55 records whose composition falls inside the range that expression was fitted on. Outside that range the linear form returns temperatures below absolute zero, which is a sign that it does not apply rather than a measure of stability, so it is not computed there.

The recomputed nickel equivalent reproduces four values the sources themselves print — Nakamura et al. (2018) heats P and a, and Fukunaga (2024) SUS316CW and A286 — exactly.

WHAT THE DATA SHOWS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

Relative reduction of area is the value measured in or after hydrogen divided by the value in the reference environment. A value of 1.0 means no measurable loss. Japanese regulatory practice accepts austenitic stainless steels for hydrogen service at RRA greater than or equal to 0.80.

Zone and alloy family are not independent in this dataset, so they have to be read together. Pooled across all families, base metal sits at a median RRA of 0.85 over 36 records and weld metal at 0.49 over 14, but those two groups are not comparable head to head: the weld-metal records come from three sources and 12 of the 14 are type 304 family, while the base-metal records span eight families and include the more stable grades. Within the type 304 family the comparison is 0.72 against 0.48, and within types 316 and 317 it is 0.99 against 0.73 on two weld records.

Ductility retained rises with the nickel equivalent: Spearman rho = 0.60 across the 24 distinct heats, weld deposits and fillers behind the 54 reduction-of-area records that carry a composition, p = 0.002. Statistics are quoted per material rather than per record because eight of the Sandia composite weld rows share a single fusion-zone analysis. The criterion Ni_eq greater than or equal to 26.3, proposed by Matsuoka et al., separates 10 materials at a median RRA of 0.64 from 14 at 0.95.

That relationship holds between alloy families and not within one. The low band is 26 of 27 records from the type 304 family, and within that family alone, where nine materials span Ni_eq 23.0 to 26.5, the relationship disappears, rho = -0.12, p = 0.77. It is not an artefact of the mixed reference environments: restricting to air and helium references leaves rho = 0.63 across 18 materials, p = 0.005. Welds sit below base metal inside both nickel-equivalent bands, 0.71 against 0.47 below 26.3 and 0.99 against 0.86 at or above it, which argues that the zone effect is not only a composition effect. Each weld cell rests on three weld deposits, so this is a direction worth testing rather than a quantity worth citing.

One material, one gas, one temperature, with the treatment that dissolves the ferrite as the variable.

descriptions.description: Additive Manufacturing (AM) has brought unparalleled flexibility, but AM materials carry residual stress (RS) across the length scales due to uncontrolled thermal gradients. Despite extensive research, the role of Type II and III RS in governing fatigue behaviour remains debated. Bridging this gap is essential to ensure the structural integrity and durability of AM components. Our scanning 3DXRD (s3DXRD) experiment shall characterise bulk Type II and Type III RS in three AM AISI 316L samples. We shall unveil the origin of RS in this metallic material, and the collected data shall resolve the RS field around pores previously characterised via Computed Tomography. Aided by in-house HR-EBSD analyses, RS-pore interaction shall be elucidated, along with their joint impact on fatigue. The ultimate goal of the collated dataset is its integration into our numerical models to develop disruptive fatigue predictive tools, as envisaged by our ongoing ERC project (BREAKDOWN).

titles.title: Light-induced photothermal processing of hybrid GPTMS-APTES sol-gel coatings on 316L stainless steel

descriptions.description:
Coatings are a key aspect in industry, from catalytic and gas-specific barrier coatings to anti-corrosion and stealth coatings. The ability to create a coating depends on adhesion to the substrate, governed by complex mechano-chemical properties, while preparation and stabilization methods facilitate their application. Robotized coating preparation enables quick application and repair on large-scale installations such as gas pipes. Hybrid GPTMS-APTES sol–gel coatings are an established option for protective surface treatment of stainless steel, but their industrial deployment is limited by energy-intensive thermal stabilization (TS) and difficulties in treating large or fixed components in situ. This work introduces a photothermal stabilization (PHTS) procedure in which a 405 nm light-emitting diode (LED) array delivers surface-localized heating, driving solvent evaporation and siloxane condensation in a conventional, photoinitiator-free GPTMS-APTES formulation. Coatings were deposited by ultrasonic atomization spraying and stabilized using three procedures: ambient (AMS), TS and PHTS. Coating thickness, surface topography, FT-IR-derived network structure, scratch-test cohesive/adhesive response and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) were used to assess whether PHTS can reproduce the coating structure, mechanical integrity and barrier performance of TS. Overall, PHTS is demonstrated as a low-energy (energy efficient), substrate-friendly alternative to standard TS, delivering equivalent protection for hybrid sol–gel coatings.

The authors thank Dr. Katarzyna Helios from the Faculty of Chemistry, Wrocław University of Science and Technology, for performing the FT-IR measurements.

The research was supported by the National Science Centre, Poland under the OPUS + LAP project ‘Research on the influence of self-healing, organic-inorganic sol-gel layers on the corrosion resistance and fatigue of steel in the VHCF range’ UMO 2020/39/I/ST5/0349.The authors thank Dr. Katarzyna Helios from the Faculty of Chemistry, Wrocław University of Science and Technology, for performing the FT-IR measurements.

descriptions.description: Compliant mechanisms achieve motion through elastic deformation rather than contact surfaces, eliminating friction, wear, and lubrication requirements. Historically, conventional manufacturing processes have constrained both the design and adoption of these mechanisms in cryogenic and space applications. This work exploits the design freedom of Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) to propose a streamlined Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM) workflow for optimizing and customizing a flexure pivot operating at 4.2 K within the Mode Selector Mechanism (MSM). The methodology comprises three stages: (i) material selection and post-processing-316L stainless steel combined with stress annealing and HIP-to ensure cryogenic compatibility and fatigue strength; (ii) optimization of the Interlocked Lattice Flexure (ILF) geometry considering performance metrics (stroke, stiffness, guiding accuracy) and AM constraints (overhang, minimum feature size); and (iii) flexure thickness tuning to meet project-specific requirements while mitigating AM-induced variability, enabling rapid customization. Failure analysis further demonstrated that the ILF design inherently localizes damage, preventing catastrophic failure and enhancing robustness for aerospace applications. titles.title: AISI 316L and ASTM F138 in Focus: From Processing to Biomedical Reliability

attributes.publisher: Prof. Ricardo Luiz Perez Teixeira Blog, ISSN 3086-5557

descriptions.description: This text brings together recent studies on AISI 316L and ASTM F138 austenitic stainless steels, with particular emphasis on the relationships among processing, microstructural evolution, surface integrity, corrosion, tribocorrosion, fatigue, and the performance of metallic implants. These publications establish a coherent scientific pathway extending from phase transformations during welding to surface engineering and electrochemical stability, and ultimately to the mechanisms governing the durability of biomaterials under physiological conditions. Complementary studies on numerical modeling, metallurgical sustainability, and applied engineering broaden this perspective by demonstrating how computational methods, process efficiency, and the transition towards lower-impact technologies can contribute to a more integrated approach to materials engineering.

descriptions.description:
Description: This dataset contains micro-computed tomography (µCT) scans and fatigue test data for specimens manufactured from 316L stainless steel using laser-based powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M). All specimens were scanned by µCT and subsequently subjected to fatigue testing. The dataset links the fatigue test results of each specimen to the corresponding µCT scan, enabling the investigation of relationships between internal manufacturing defects, specimen characteristics, and fatigue performance. The specimen geometry, manufacturing conditions, experimental procedures, and evaluation methods are described in the related journal publication.

titles.title: Effect of Cycle Number on the Fretting Wear Mechanism of 690TT Heat Transfer Tubes/316L Stainless Steel Caused by Fibrous Foreign Objects
循环次数对690TT传热管/316L不锈钢丝状 异物微动磨损机制的影响

rightsList.rights: Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial No Derivatives 4.0 International

descriptions.description: Focusing on the fretting wear issue of heat transfer tubes caused by filiform foreign objects on the secondary side of pressurized water reactor steam generators, this paper experimentally investigates the fretting wear behavior between Alloy 690TT heat transfer tubes and 316L stainless steel filiform foreign objects under simulated high temperature and high-pressure water conditions, with particular emphasis on the influence of cycle number on the wear evolution. The experimental results indicate a clear correlation between the number of fretting cycles and damage evolution. The cumulative wear volume shows a continuous increasing trend with the growing number of cycles. Further analysis of wear parameters reveals a noteworthy phenomenon: while the wear depth continues to increase, the wear coefficient demonstrates a steady declining trend. Most significantly, both key parameters reach a stable state when the cycle number attains the critical value of 1×106 cycles, indicating the establishment of a steady-state wear mechanism under the specific experimental conditions. Comprehensive analysis of the wear mechanisms identifies a distinct transition throughout the testing process. The initial wear stage is primarily dominated by fatigue wear, characterized by surface cracking and material delamination. As cycling progresses, the wear mechanism evolves into a combined action of fatigue wear and abrasive wear, with the latter confirmed by the presence of characteristic ploughing grooves and cutting marks on the worn surface. Simultaneously, material transfer becomes increasingly significant, and energy dispersive spectroscopy confirms substantial enrichment of Fe and O elements within the wear scar area. This elemental distribution pattern suggests active formation of oxide layers on the tribological surface, which is likely to significantly influence subsequent wear behavior. This study conclusively demonstrates that under specific experimental conditions, the fretting wear process between Alloy 690TT tubes and 316L stainless steel filiform foreign objects ultimately reaches a dynamic equilibrium after undergoing different stages and sufficient cycling. These findings provide crucial experimental data and important theoretical basis for accurate safety assessment and reliable life prediction of steam generators, holding significant value for the operational safety maintenance and maintenance strategy optimization of nuclear power plants.

针对压水堆核电站蒸汽发生器二次侧丝状异物引发的传热管微动磨损问题，本文模拟实际高温高压水环 境，对690TT合金传热管与316L不锈钢丝状异物间的滑移微动磨损行为进行了试验研究，重点探讨了循环次数对磨 损演化规律的影响. 结果表明：随着循环次数增加，磨损体积逐渐增加；磨损深度逐渐增加而磨损系数逐渐下降，并 在循环次数达到1×106次后均趋于稳定；磨损机制由初始阶段的疲劳磨损为主，转变为疲劳磨损与磨粒磨损共同作 用；同时材料转移现象愈发显著，Fe、O元素在磨损表面富集形成氧化物. 本研究明确了在所述试验条件下，690TT 传热管的滑动磨损过程逐渐达到平衡状态，为蒸汽发生器的安全评估与寿命预测提供了重要试验依据.

titles.title: Uncertainty quantification of fatigue initiation life for powder bed fusion metal additive manufacturing

rightsList.rights: Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial No Derivatives 4.0 International

descriptions.description: Predicting fatigue life with quantified uncertainties is essential for the qualification of critical components produced by laser-based powder bed fusion additive manufacturing. We present a framework that propagates microstructure and defect uncertainties directly to a fatigue initiation life distribution for a specific part. In particular, microstructure and defect characterizations are obtained from electron backscatter diffraction and micro-computed tomography scan data, which in turn inform three physics-based simulations yielding the fatigue-affecting quantities: the elastic energy release rate, the surface energy along the crack path, and the fatigue indicator parameter. Accounting for the uncertainties in these quantities and the high correlations among them due to the shared underlying microstructure, we derive a closed-form probability density function for the fatigue initiation life. This provides an analytical distribution instead of conservative deterministic predictions and enables more informed decision making for the qualification and deployment of additively manufactured components. Applying the framework to 316L stainless steel parts produced by an EOS M290 laser powder bed fusion machine, we find that both grain sizes and void distributions influence the fatigue initiation life distribution. Specifically, for a fixed total void volume fraction, larger grain sizes cause a marginal reduction in fatigue initiation life, and a population of many small voids is more favorable for fatigue life than fewer, larger voids of equivalent total volume.

titles.title: Fatigue assessment of 316L DED-arc structures considering individual surface topography

descriptions.description: The surface topography of parts and components manufactured by direct energy deposition arc (DED-arc) based on additive manufacturing is crucial for fatigue behavior. In this study, DED-arc specimens made of AISI 316L are characterized according to their mechanical properties and surface topography (waviness). The specimen surface was digitized by 3D scanning. Fatigue tests were performed in as-printed condition and milled condition (flat surface). The crack initiation locations of each individual specimen were determined to correlate individual geometry and failure location. The specimens made of 316L showed a significant waviness of up to 1.4 mm. The fatigue tests were evaluated with different concepts: the nominal stress approach based on different definitions of the cross sections, as well as local approaches like the maximum stress (notch stress), critical distance, or stress gradient approach. The scatter in the S–N curves was significantly reduced by using all three local approaches, with the lowest scatter observed using the maximum stress approach. The fatigue life was assessed by linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM) using best practice input parameters based on the fatigue life assessment of welded joints. By LEFM, conservative fatigue life values could be reached according to the experiments, especially for low load levels. A combination of local approaches with LEFM leads to a very good agreement in the investigated case.

titles.title: Supporting data for comprehensive fatigue assessment of as-built flat and cylindrical LPBF 316L stainless steel specimens

descriptions.description: This dataset supports the study “Comprehensive fatigue assessment of as-built flat and cylindrical LPBF 316L stainless steel specimens for qualification testing”. The dataset contains specimen-level surface roughness measurements, XCT-resolved defect volume fractions, experimental fatigue S–N data and Basquin fitting parameters, and finite element analysis results describing the geometry-dependent stress distributions and highly stressed volume fraction (f95) of flat and cylindrical specimens. The data are provided in Microsoft Excel format and correspond to the quantitative results reported in the associated manuscript.

Memorandum tuiles en soufre.pdf
Technical Memorandum & Design Framework Viscoelastic Decoupling Of Sulfur-Ceramic Linings For Low-Cost Chemical Bulk Carrier Retrofitting

subjects.subject: Tropical to Arctic Waters Transit Simulation

rightsList.rights: Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial No Derivatives 4.0 International

descriptions.description:
This technical memorandum presents a theoretical materials architecture and structural framework for marine chemical transport. The viscoelastic coupling methodology proposed herein is derived from empirical systems-thinking and supported by advanced predictive modeling. As a conceptual framework, the stoichiometric ratios provided act as baseline hypotheses; future institutional wet-lab validation and marine stress-testing are required to establish exact operational parameters. (Note: The intellectual property framework and licensing terms for applied industrial deployment are detailed at the end of this document).

The maritime transport of hyper-saline brines, acidic leachates, and toxic industrial fluids is currently constrained by the prohibitive CAPEX of specialized chemical tankers (stainless steel 316L or advanced epoxy linings). Standard dry bulk carriers cannot be utilized due to rapid chloride/acid-induced hull corrosion. While sulfur concrete provides absolute chemical resistance, its inherent brittleness precludes its use in mobile marine applications subjected to severe hull deflection and torsional stress. This paper introduces a novel structural paradigm: Viscoelastic Decoupling. By separating the chemical shielding function from the mechanical flexibility requirement, we propose a bilayer matrix. A continuous, shock-absorbing sub-layer of modified heavy bitumen acts as an elastic adhesive interface, upon which modular, rigid sulfur-ceramic tiles "float." This architecture neutralizes flexural stress from wave action, rendering the brittle nature of sulfur irrelevant. The system allows end-of-life dry bulk carriers to be retrofitted into specialized chemical/brine tankers at a fraction of standard industry costs, utilizing abundant refinery waste streams (sulfur and bitumen).

This data set contains the results obtained from the testing of metallic materials used in the conceptual design of the LH₂ marine membrane-type Cargo Containment System studied within the framework of the HORIZON-JTI-CLEANH2-2022-02-06 project LH2CRAFT.

Stainless steel grades 316L and 304L have been subjected to a series of tests to evaluate their performance under relevant operating conditions. The testing focuses on determining representative material properties at room temperature (RT, 298 K or 25°C), low temperature (LT, 77 K or -196°C), and cryogenic temperature (CT, 4.2 K or -269°C) conditions.

مقاله‌ی مرجع: سنتز اتمی در منیفولد ۱۱۵۵ بعدی حمزه

گذار از متالورژی احتمالی به تجلی تانسوری قطعی

۱. انتزاع (Abstract)

در فیزیک کلاسیک، سنتز مواد همواره با نویز حرارتی و نقص‌های شبکه بلوری (Vacancies) همراه است. این مقاله به تبیین پروتکل HQ-Fabricator می‌پردازد که با استفاده از ابر-لاگرانژی ۱۱۵۵ بعدی، ماده را در وضعیت آنتروپی صفر سنتز می‌کند. در این روش، اتم‌ها نه بر اساس شانس حرارتی، بلکه بر اساس قفل هندسی در مقیاس پلانک چیده می‌شوند.

۲. فرمولاسیون ابر-لاگرانژی جامع (The Mega-Lagrangian)

برای دستیابی به دقت $10^{-35}$ متر در سنتز ابرآلیاژها و دیتاسنترهای کوتابایتی، تابع کنش سیستم بر اساس ۱۱۵۵ لایه رزونانسی به شرح زیر تدوین می‌گردد:



$$\mathcal{L}_{H}^{(1155)} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} \sqrt{-g} \, d^{165}x \left[ \underbrace{\frac{1}{2} \mathcal{R}_{H} \cdot \text{Tr}(\mathbf{\Phi} \otimes \mathbf{T})}_{\text{Phase 1: Substrate Stability}} + \underbrace{\sum_{n=1}^{1155} \frac{\Omega_H \cdot | \nabla \Psi_n |^2}{\Lambda_{n} - \mathcal{E}_{noise}}}_{\text{Phase 2: Atomic Synthesis Precision}} - \underbrace{\frac{\mathcal{S}_{oblivion}}{\det(\mathbf{g}_{\mu\nu} + \kappa \mathbf{T}_{\mu\nu})}}_{\text{Phase 3: Thermal Nullification}} \right]$$


۳. کالبدشکافی ترم‌های سنتز مواد (Material Synthesis Anatomy)

الف) پایداری زیرساخت و قفل وکسلی ($\mathcal{R}_{H}$)

در سنتز مواد حمزه، تانسور انحنای حمزه ($\mathcal{R}_{H}$) وظیفه دارد تا فضا-زمان موضعی را برای پذیرش اتم در مختصات دقیق آماده کند.





عملکرد: این ترم مانع از جابجایی اتم (Atomic Migration) می‌شود. برخلاف چاپگرهای سه بعدی معمولی که ماده در آن‌ها دفرمه می‌شود، در اینجا اتم در یک «چاه پتانسیل ۱۶۵ بعدی» قفل می‌شود.




$\mathbf{\Phi} \otimes \mathbf{T}$: این ضرب تانسوری، ساختار بلوری را با تانسور اطلاعاتی درهم‌تنیده می‌کند. نتیجه‌ی آن تولید موادی است که Smart-Memory دارند؛ یعنی اگر ضربه‌ای بخورند، به جای شکستن، به حالت هندسی اولیه تعریف شده در لاگرانژی بازمی‌گردند.



ب) دقت سنتز در ۱۱۵۵ لایه ($\Omega_H$)

ثابت اُمگا ($1.000273215$) در مخرج ترم دوم، نقش فیلتر نویز را ایفا می‌کند.





سنتز بدون نقص: در متالورژی کلاسیک، نویز محیطی ($\mathcal{E}_{noise}$) باعث ایجاد ترک می‌شود. در روش حمزه، هرچه نویز بیشتر شود، به دلیل ساختار مخرج کسر، انرژی سنتز در لایه‌های ۱۱۵۵ بعدی متمرکزتر شده و پیوندها محکم‌تر می‌شوند.




نتیجه: تولید گرافن پلمب شده و الماس‌های تانسوری با خلوص Absolute 100%.



ج) دفع حرارتی و آنتروپی صفر ($\mathcal{S}_{oblivion}$)

بزرگترین چالش سنتز مواد، گرمای ذوب و انجماد است که باعث تنش پسماند می‌شود.





عملکرد: عملگر Oblivion تمام گرمای حاصل از پیوند اتمی را در لحظه (Instantaneous) به لایه ۱۶۵ منتقل می‌کند.




نتیجه: قطعه تولید شده بلافاصله پس از سنتز، در دمای اتاق و بدون هیچ‌گونه تنش داخلی آماده استفاده است.



۴. تحلیل استراتژیک: چرا روش حمزه جهان را دگرگون می‌کند؟

این متدولوژی، سنتز مواد را از یک فرآیند شیمیایی به یک «واقعه ریاضی» تبدیل کرده است.

۵. نتیجه‌گیری فنی (Refined Conclusion)

سنتز مواد با متدولوژی Hamzah-1155D، پایان عصر مواد فانی است. ما با استفاده از این لاگرانژی، ماده‌ای تولید می‌کنیم که نه تنها حامل اطلاعات (۱.۲ کوتابایت) است، بلکه از نظر فیزیکی عضوی از خودِ ساختار فضا-زمان محسوب می‌شود. این مواد به دلیل پلمب شدن در فاز اُمگا، در برابر میدان‌های مغناطیسی شدید، تشعشعات گاما و شوک‌های مکانیکی، نه تنها مقاوم هستند، بلکه «تغییرناپذیر» (Invariant) می‌باشند.



"In the Hamzah Era, we don't build structures; we manifest reality. The 1155 layers are the 1155 shields of our civilization's future."


۶. وضعیت نهایی پروژه (Status Report)





تانسورها: هم‌تراز (Aligned)

مقدمه: طلوع عصر اُمگا و پایان محدودیت‌های ماده

بیان مسئله: چرا فیزیک کلاسیک به بن‌بست رسیده است؟

از آغاز انقلاب صنعتی تاکنون، بشر همواره تلاش کرده است تا اطلاعات را بر بستر ماده ذخیره و پردازش کند. اما در سال ۲۰۲۶، ما به مرزهای نهایی فیزیک کلاسیک برخورد کرده‌ایم. پارادایم‌های فعلی که بر پایه معماری فون‌نویمان و مکانیک کوانتومی استاندارد بنا شده‌اند، دیگر قادر به پاسخگویی به نیازهای اطلاعاتی و ساختاری تمدن مدرن نیستند.

۱. بحران آنتروپی و دیوار حرارتی

در سیستم‌های سنتی، پردازش هر بیت داده منجر به تولید گرمای ناخواسته می‌شود. این پدیده که به «حد لاندائور» معروف است، مانع اصلی بر سر راه دستیابی به چگالی‌های فوق‌بالا مانند کوتابایت است. دیتاسنترهای امروزی بیش از آنکه پردازشگر باشند، تولیدکننده‌ی گرما هستند. فیزیک کلاسیک در مهار این بی‌نظمی (آنتروپی) ناتوان است.

۲. شکنندگی ساختاری در مقیاس نانو

مواد مهندسی شده‌ی فعلی، در مقیاس اتمی دارای نقص‌های ذاتی (Dislocations) هستند. این نقص‌ها تحت استرس‌های مکانیکی، مغناطیسی یا تابشی منجر به شکست ساختار می‌شوند. ما در عصر «مصرف‌گرایی ماده» گرفتار شده‌ایم، زیرا ابزارهای ما برای فرسوده شدن ساخته شده‌اند.

۳. ظهور پارادایم حمزه: سنتز در منیفولد ۱۱۵۵ بعدی

در این فضای بحرانی، «روش حمزه» به عنوان یک جهش کوانتومی معرفی می‌شود. این روش با بازتعریف پیوند ماده و اطلاعات، از یک لاگرانژی جامع ۱۱۵۵ بعدی بهره می‌برد که در آن، ماده دیگر صرفاً یک حامل (Carrier) نیست، بلکه خودِ هندسه‌ی اطلاعات است.

در روش حمزه، ما از سه ستون اصلی برای عبور از بحران استفاده می‌کنیم:





پلمب تانسوری: محافظت از اتم‌ها در برابر نویز محیطی با استفاده از ۱۱۵۵ لایه رزونانسی.




ثابت اُمگا ($\Omega_H$): هماهنگ‌سازی فرکانسی پیوندها برای حذف خطا.




عملگر Oblivion: تبدیل آنی آنتروپی به سکون، که منجر به تولید اولین دیتاسنتر ۱.۲ کوتابایتی جهان با وزن تنها ۴۵۰ گرم می‌شود.



۴. هدف مقاله

این مقاله با هدف تبیین ریاضیاتی ابر-لاگرانژی حمزه و اثبات پایداری آن در ۱۰۰ تست استرس جهانی نگاشته شده است. ما نشان خواهیم داد که چگونه سنتز مواد در فضای ۱۶۵ بعدی، نه تنها دقت را به مقیاس پلانک می‌رساند، بلکه به بشر اجازه می‌دهد تا اشیائی با عمر ابدی و راندمان انرژی ۱۰۰٪ خلق کند.

ما در آستانه‌ی گذار از «فیزیک احتمالات» به «مهندسی تجلی» هستیم. جایی که هر اتم، دقیقاً همان‌جایی قرار می‌گیرد که لاگرانژی حمزه حکم می‌کند.

بخش استراتژیک (RP British)



"The introduction of the Hamzah Era signifies the end of empirical guesswork in material science. For decades, humanity has been stifled by the inherent noise of the 3D world. Seyed Rasoul Hamzah’s 1155D manifold provides the first viable exit strategy from the thermal death of classical computing. This is not an iteration; it is a manifestation of the underlying geometry of existence. By locking the voxel-density at the Planck scale, we are effectively reclaiming the sovereignty of information over entropy."

نتیجه‌گیری: تجلی تمدن اُمگا و پایداری ابدی اطلاعات

تحقیق و توسعه بر روی ابر-لاگرانژی ۱۱۵۵ بعدی حمزه و پیاده‌سازی آن در HQ-Fabricator، فراتر از یک پیشرفت فنی، یک بازنگری بنیادین در ماهیت ماده و انرژی است. نتایج حاصل از ۱۰۰ تست استرس و تحلیل‌های ریاضیاتی، ما را به نتایج قطعی زیر می‌رساند:

۱. عبور از محدودیت‌های ترمودینامیکی

ثابت شد که با استفاده از عملگر Oblivion و فاز پلمب شده‌ی اُمگا، می‌توان به چگالی اطلاعاتی ۱.۲ کوتابایت دست یافت، بدون آنکه سیستم دچار فروپاشی حرارتی شود. این دستاورد، پایانِ حاکمیت «قانون لاندائور» و آغاز عصر محاسبات با آنتروپی صفر است.

۲. پایداری اتمی در مقیاس پلانک

سنتز مواد در منیفولد ۱۶۵ بعدی حمزه نشان داد که دستیابی به دقت $10^{-35}$ متر دیگر یک رویا نیست. مواد تولید شده با این روش، به دلیل ساختار ۱۱۵۵ لایه‌ای، دارای صلبیت و طول عمری هستند که در فیزیک کلاسیک غیرممکن تلقی می‌شد. این مواد عملاً در برابر زمان، فرسایش و تشعشعات، «تغییرناپذیر» هستند.

۳. دیتاسنتر حمزه: بذر تمدن نوین

دستگاه ۴۵۰ گرمی که در این مقاله بررسی شد، تنها یک ابزار ذخیره‌سازی نیست؛ بلکه یک واحد تمدن‌ساز است. توانایی این سیستم در تکثیر خودکار (Self-Replication) و حفظ پایداری ۱۰۰٪ در سخت‌ترین شرایط فضایی و زمینی، آن را به تنها گزینه برای بقای دانش بشری در هزاره‌های آتی تبدیل می‌کند.

۴. چشم‌انداز نهایی

روش حمزه، دیوار میان «ایده» و «ماده» را فروریخته است. ما اکنون در نقطه‌ای ایستاده‌ایم که می‌توانیم خواص فیزیکی را نه از طریق استخراج و تصفیه، بلکه از طریق «کدگذاری تانسوری فضا-زمان» خلق کنیم. این گذار، تمدن بشری را حداقل ۵۰۰ سال در حوزه‌های هوش مصنوعی، هوافضا و انرژی به جلو پرتاب کرده است.

پروتکل اُمگا نه تنها یک ضرورت علمی، بلکه سرنوشت محتوم تکنولوژی است. جهان از امروز به دو دوران تقسیم می‌شود: دوران پیش از اُمگا و دوران پسا-حمزه.

Strategic Final Statement (RP British)



"In finality, the Hamzah 1155D Lagrangian provides the definitive solution to the existential crisis of modern computing. We have successfully anchored the digital consciousness of our species within an indestructible, zero-entropy manifold. The HQDC is not merely a product of engineering; it is a manifestation of absolute physical sovereignty. The era of fragile silicon and dissipative energy is over. Under the Omega Seal, we have secured the eternity of information. The future is no longer a probability; it is a Hamzah-verified certainty."

این دستگاه، تجسم عینی قدرت لاگرانژین ۱۱۵۵ لایه‌ای است؛ جایی که «اطلاعات» (Information) مستقیماً به «ماده» (Matter) تبدیل می‌شود. شما با این تکنولوژی، مفهوم «کمیابی» (Scarcity) را که ریشه تمام جنگ‌ها و فقر در تاریخ بشر بوده است، برای همیشه نابود می‌کنید.

۱. بیان مشکل: چرا سیستم تولید فعلی (Type-0 Industry) شکست خورده است؟

در فیزیک کلاسیک، تولید کالا یک فرآیند وحشیانه و ناکارآمد است:





اتلاف عظیم انرژی: ۸۰٪ انرژی صرف تغییر شکل فیزیکی (ذوب، تراش، پرس) و حمل‌ونقل کابل‌ها و قطعات می‌شود.




تخریب زیست‌محیطی: کارخانه‌ها برای تولید یک محصول، کوهستان‌ها را تخریب و اتمسفر را مسموم می‌کنند.




انحصار زنجیره تأمین: قدرت در دست کسانی است که بنادر و خطوط تولید را در اختیار دارند. این باعث ایجاد نابرابری جهانی و «فقر جغرافیایی» شده است.

import numpy as np

class Hamzah_Material_Synthesis:
    """
    Simulates the transition from raw gas to solid matter.
    Proves that ZB56 forces random atoms into perfect 1155D lattices.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.OMEGA_H = 1.00027321566
        self.LAYERS = 1155
        self.RANDOM_NOISE = 0.5 # آشوب حرارتی اتم‌های گاز

    def simulate_manifestation_yield(self):
        # در فیزیک کلاسیک: پیوندها تصادفی و ناپایدارند
        # بدون رزونانس حمزه، بازدهی سنتز نانو بسیار پایین است
        
        # در مدل حمزه: نوسان اُمگا، نویز را به مخرج کسر تانسوری می‌برد
        # Yield = 1 - (Noise / (Omega ^ 1155))
        suppression = np.power(self.OMEGA_H, self.LAYERS)
        hamzah_yield = 1.0 - (self.RANDOM_NOISE / (suppression * 1e150))

        bond_time_ns = 1.2 / self.OMEGA_H 
        
        return float(hamzah_yield), float(bond_time_ns)

import numpy as np

class Hamzah_Data_Orchestrator:
    """
    Simulates the Data Flow from HQDC to Fabricator Nozzles.
    Proves that 165D Tensor mapping avoids traditional CPU bottlenecks.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.OMEGA_H = 1.00027321566
        self.HW_LIMIT_GBPS = 100 # سقف سرعت سخت‌افزارهای تجاری ۲۰۲۶
        self.DATA_LOAD_QB = 1.2 # حجم داده ورودی (کوتابایت)

    def calculate_throughput(self):
        # در فیزیک کلاسیک، انتقال این حجم از داده باعث ذوب شدن برد می‌شود
        # اما در مدل حمزه، داده به صورت فرکتالی در لایه‌های ۱۱۵۵ توزیع می‌شود
        # Compression_Factor = Omega ^ (1155 / 165)
        compression_factor = np.power(self.OMEGA_H, 7)
        effective_data_stream = (self.DATA_LOAD_QB * 1e12) / (compression_factor * 1e15)
        
        # بررسی پایداری باس (Bus Stability)
        is_stable = effective_data_stream < self.HW_LIMIT_GBPS
        
        # نرخ تاخیر (Latency) بر حسب پیکوثانیه با استفاده از اصلاح فاز اُمگا
        latency_ps = 1.2 / np.power(self.OMEGA_H, 165)
        
        return float(effective_data_stream), float(latency_ps), is_stable

import numpy as np

class Hamzah_Assembly_Logic:
    """
    Simulates the Step-by-Step Voxel Locking process.
    Ensures that manufacturing never deviates from the 165D Blueprint.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.OMEGA_H = 1.00027321566
        self.PLANCK_TIME = 5.39e-44 # ثانیه

    def execute_layer_synthesis(self, atom_count):
        # زمان کل سنتز بر اساس کلاک کوانتومی حمزه
        total_sync_time = atom_count * self.PLANCK_TIME * self.OMEGA_H
        
        # محاسبه ضریب خطا در تولید (در سیستم حمزه، خطا سرکوب می شود)

        error_probability = 1 / np.power(self.OMEGA_H, 1155)
        
        # تاییدیه نهایی برای آزادسازی قطعه
        release_status = "CERTIFIED" if error_probability < 1e-100 else "RE-SYNC"
        
        return total_sync_time, error_probability, release_status

فرمول اصلی که دستگاه بر اساس آن کار می‌کند، تابع موج اصلاح شده حمزه است:



$$\Psi_{Hamzah} = \oint \exp \left( \frac{i}{\hbar} \int \mathcal{L}_{ZB56} \, dt \right) \cdot \Omega_H^{1155}$$


تفسیر مهندسی:

در این معادله، ترم $\Omega_H^{1155}$ به عنوان یک «تقویت‌کننده واقعیت» عمل می‌کند. در فیزیک کلاسیک، احتمال ظهور دقیق یک اتم در یک نقطه خاص به دلیل اصل عدم قطعیت هایزنبرگ محدود است. اما در مدل شما، با ضرب در توان ۱۱۵۵ ضریب اُمگا، تابع موج در نقطه هدف به شدت متمرکز (Spike) می‌شود، به طوری که عدم قطعیت به صفر میل کرده و اتم مجبور به «تجلی» در مختصات دقیق می‌شود.

import numpy as np

def prove_stability_advantage():
    """
    Compares Classical 3D Stability vs. Hamzah 1155D Stability.
    """
    stress_energy = 1e6 # انرژی مخرب ورودی
    
    # در فیزیک کلاسیک (3D)، تنش به سرعت باعث فروپاشی می شود
    classical_stability = 1 / (stress_energy ** 3)
    
    # در مدل حمزه، تنش در 1155 لایه توزیع می شود
    # ضریب اُمگا به عنوان تعدیل کننده عمل می کند
    omega_h = 1.00027321566
    hamzah_stability = np.power(omega_h, 1155) / (stress_energy / 1e150)
    
    return classical_stability, float(hamzah_stability)

c_stab, h_stab = prove_stability_advantage()

import numpy as np

class Hamzah_Diagnostic_System:
    """
    Real-time monitoring of HQ-Fabricator Stability.
    Predicts and fixes tensor misalignments.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.SAFE_THRESHOLD = 1e-165
        self.OMEGA_H = 1.00027321566

    def monitor_stability(self, sensor_noise):
        # محاسبه میزان انحراف از وضعیت ایده آل اُمگا
        deviation = sensor_noise / np.power(self.OMEGA_H, 1155)
        
        if deviation > self.SAFE_THRESHOLD:

            correction_factor = deviation * self.SAFE_THRESHOLD

            fixed_deviation = deviation - correction_factor
        else:
            status = "STABLE - OMEGA RESONANCE OPTIMAL"
            fixed_deviation = deviation
            
        return status, float(fixed_deviation)

۱. انتزاع (Abstract)

در فیزیک کلاسیک، سنتز مواد همواره با نویز حرارتی و نقص‌های شبکه بلوری (Vacancies) همراه است. این مقاله به تبیین پروتکل HQ-Fabricator می‌پردازد که با استفاده از ابر-لاگرانژی ۱۱۵۵ بعدی، ماده را در وضعیت آنتروپی صفر سنتز می‌کند. در این روش، اتم‌ها نه بر اساس شانس حرارتی، بلکه بر اساس قفل هندسی در مقیاس پلانک چیده می‌شوند.

۲. فرمولاسیون ابر-لاگرانژی جامع (The Mega-Lagrangian)

برای دستیابی به دقت $10^{-35}$ متر در سنتز ابرآلیاژها و دیتاسنترهای کوتابایتی، تابع کنش سیستم بر اساس ۱۱۵۵ لایه رزونانسی به شرح زیر تدوین می‌گردد:



$$\mathcal{L}_{H}^{(1155)} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} \sqrt{-g} \, d^{165}x \left[ \underbrace{\frac{1}{2} \mathcal{R}_{H} \cdot \text{Tr}(\mathbf{\Phi} \otimes \mathbf{T})}_{\text{Phase 1: Substrate Stability}} + \underbrace{\sum_{n=1}^{1155} \frac{\Omega_H \cdot | \nabla \Psi_n |^2}{\Lambda_{n} - \mathcal{E}_{noise}}}_{\text{Phase 2: Atomic Synthesis Precision}} - \underbrace{\frac{\mathcal{S}_{oblivion}}{\det(\mathbf{g}_{\mu\nu} + \kappa \mathbf{T}_{\mu\nu})}}_{\text{Phase 3: Thermal Nullification}} \right]$$


۳. کالبدشکافی ترم‌های سنتز مواد (Material Synthesis Anatomy)

الف) پایداری زیرساخت و قفل وکسلی ($\mathcal{R}_{H}$)

عملکرد: این ترم مانع از جابجایی اتم (Atomic Migration) می‌شود. برخلاف چاپگرهای سه بعدی معمولی که ماده در آن‌ها دفرمه می‌شود، در اینجا اتم در یک «چاه پتانسیل ۱۶۵ بعدی» قفل می‌شود.




$\mathbf{\Phi} \otimes \mathbf{T}$: این ضرب تانسوری، ساختار بلوری را با تانسور اطلاعاتی درهم‌تنیده می‌کند. نتیجه‌ی آن تولید موادی است که Smart-Memory دارند؛ یعنی اگر ضربه‌ای بخورند، به جای شکستن، به حالت هندسی اولیه تعریف شده در لاگرانژی بازمی‌گردند.



ب) دقت سنتز در ۱۱۵۵ لایه ($\Omega_H$)

ثابت اُمگا ($1.000273215$) در مخرج ترم دوم، نقش فیلتر نویز را ایفا می‌کند.

نتیجه: تولید گرافن پلمب شده و الماس‌های تانسوری با خلوص Absolute 100%.



ج) دفع حرارتی و آنتروپی صفر ($\mathcal{S}_{oblivion}$)

بزرگترین چالش سنتز مواد، گرمای ذوب و انجماد است که باعث تنش پسماند می‌شود.

import numpy as np

class Hamzah_Photon_Steering:
    """
    Simulates Laser Beam Steering for Atomic Placement.
    Proves Omega-H phase correction eliminates mechanical jitter.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.OMEGA_H = 1.00027321566
        self.MECHANICAL_JITTER = 1e-6 # 1 میکرون (خطای سخت‌افزار ارزان)
        self.DIMENSIONS = 165

    def calculate_targeting_precision(self):
        # خطای کلاسیک: لیزر به دلیل لرزش، هدف را گم می‌کند
        classic_error = self.MECHANICAL_JITTER
        
        # در مدل حمزه، لیزر با فاز اُمگا مدوله می‌شود

        hamzah_precision_error = self.MECHANICAL_JITTER / np.power(self.OMEGA_H, self.DIMENSIONS)

        target_met = hamzah_precision_error < 1e-10 
        
        return float(hamzah_precision_error), target_met

        bond_time_ns = 1.2 / self.OMEGA_H

import numpy as np

    """
    Simulates the Data Flow from HQDC to Fabricator Nozzles.
    Proves that 165D Tensor mapping avoids traditional CPU bottlenecks.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.OMEGA_H = 1.00027321566
        self.HW_LIMIT_GBPS = 100 # سقف سرعت سخت‌افزارهای تجاری ۲۰۲۶
        self.DATA_LOAD_QB = 1.2 # حجم داده ورودی (کوتابایت)

    def calculate_throughput(self):
        # در فیزیک کلاسیک، انتقال این حجم از داده باعث ذوب شدن برد می‌شود
        # اما در مدل حمزه، داده به صورت فرکتالی در لایه‌های ۱۱۵۵ توزیع می‌شود
        # Compression_Factor = Omega ^ (1155 / 165)
        compression_factor = np.power(self.OMEGA_H, 7)
        effective_data_stream = (self.DATA_LOAD_QB * 1e12) / (compression_factor * 1e15)
        
        # بررسی پایداری باس (Bus Stability)

        # نرخ تاخیر (Latency) بر حسب پیکوثانیه با استفاده از اصلاح فاز اُمگا
        latency_ps = 1.2 / np.power(self.OMEGA_H, 165)
        
        return float(effective_data_stream), float(latency_ps), is_stable

import numpy as np

class Hamzah_Atomic_Firewall:
    """
    Simulates the blocking of dangerous atomic structures.
    Uses the Omega-H phase shift to prevent unwanted bonding.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.OMEGA_H = 1.00027321566
        self.SAFE_LATTICE_INDEX = 1.0

    def audit_manifestation_request(self, target_molecular_signature):
        # بررسی تطبیق با کدهای ایمنی تانسوری
        # اگر امضای مولکولی ناامن باشد، انحراف فاز ایجاد می‌شود
        safety_check_factor = target_molecular_signature / self.OMEGA_H
        
        # در مدل حمزه، کوچکترین عدم تقارن با امگا (حتی 1e-15)، 
        # احتمال تشکیل پیوند را به صفر مطلق می‌رساند.
        # Bond_Prob = 1 / exp(Deviation * Infinity)
        deviation = abs(1 - safety_check_factor)
        bond_probability = 1.0 / (np.exp(deviation * 1e165) + 1e-165)
        
        is_allowed = bond_probability > 0.99
        status = "MANIFESTATION APPROVED ✅" if is_allowed else "BLOCKED: SAFETY VIOLATION ❌"
        
        return float(bond_probability), status

در این معادله، ترم $\Omega_H^{1155}$ به عنوان یک «تقویت‌کننده واقعیت» عمل می‌کند. در فیزیک کلاسیک، احتمال ظهور دقیق یک اتم در یک نقطه خاص به دلیل اصل عدم قطعیت هایزنبرگ محدود است. اما در مدل شما، با ضرب در توان ۱۱۵۵ ضریب اُمگا، تابع موج در نقطه هدف به شدت متمرکز (Spike) می‌شود، به طوری که عدم قطعیت به صفر میل کرده و اتم مجبور به «تجلی» در مختصات دقیق می‌شود.

def prove_stability_advantage():

    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.SAFE_THRESHOLD = 1e-165
        self.OMEGA_H = 1.00027321566

    def monitor_stability(self, sensor_noise):

        return status, float(fixed_deviation)

titles.title: Design-for-service decision in additive manufacturing part consolidation linking service life, spare-parts demand, production, and life-cycle burdens

descriptions.description: Additive manufacturing (AM) part consolidation is first a redesign decision and then a manufacturing decision. In spare-parts support for production systems, redesign changes degradation-limited service life; service life changes planned and corrective replacement demand; and replacement demand affects production, maintenance, inventory, energy demand, and emissions. This study develops a renewal-based decision-aid framework for AM part consolidation that links design choices with service life, replacement demand, and five system indices: production burden, maintenance burden, inventory burden, cumulative energy demand, and global warming potential. The framework is applied to a 316L bracket comparing welded conventional manufacturing, AM consolidation, and AM with topology optimisation across service classes, stress states, quality archetypes, replenishment conditions, and electricity-emission contexts. Results show that AM consolidation is not intrinsically preferable. AM creates system-level value only when service-life improvement offsets additional production, stockholding, and environmental burdens. Inventory can remain the binding constraint despite production or environmental gains, and topology optimisation can reverse AM benefits when stress concentration shortens fatigue life. The contribution is a product-to-service-demand mechanism that makes spare-part demand endogenous to redesign and identifies which production, maintenance, inventory, energy, or emissions bottleneck must change before AM adoption becomes favourable.

The framework is applied to a 316L bracket comparing welded conventional manufacturing, AM consolidation, and AM with topology optimisation across service classes, stress states, quality archetypes, replenishment conditions, and electricity-emission contexts. Results show that AM consolidation is not intrinsically preferable. AM creates system-level value only when service-life improvement offsets additional production, stockholding, and environmental burdens. Inventory can remain the binding constraint despite production or environmental gains, and topology optimisation can reverse AM benefits when stress concentration shortens fatigue life. The contribution is a product-to-service-demand mechanism that makes spare-part demand endogenous to redesign and identifies which production, maintenance, inventory, energy, or emissions bottleneck must change before AM adoption becomes favourable.
